questions.title: Definition of Recursion
questions.description: In Java, a method is described as recursive when:
questions.Option1: A method calls itself to solve a smaller version of the same problem
questions.Option2: A class extends another class and overrides its methods
questions.Option3: A loop repeats its body until a condition becomes false
questions.Option4: Two objects hold references to each other

questions.title: Role of the Base Case
questions.description: In a recursive method, the base case is best described as:
questions.Option1: The statement where the method calls itself with a smaller input
questions.Option2: The condition that stops the recursion and returns a value directly
questions.Option3: The variable that counts how many times the method has been called
questions.Option4: The return type chosen for the recursive method

questions.title: Call Stack Behavior During Recursion
questions.description: Each time a recursive method calls itself in Java, what does the runtime do?
questions.Option1: It overwrites the previous call's variables inside the same frame
questions.Option2: It stores all active calls in one shared memory location
questions.Option3: It pushes a new frame onto the call stack holding that call's own parameters and local variables
questions.Option4: It copies the method bytecode into a new class at runtime

questions.title: Rewriting Recursion as Iteration
questions.description: Which statement about recursion and iteration is TRUE?
questions.Option1: Any recursive solution can be rewritten with loops, though some cases then need an explicit stack for the pending work
questions.Option2: Recursion can solve problems that no loop-based program can ever solve in any form
questions.Option3: A loop can never reproduce the exact output of any recursive method
questions.Option4: Converting recursion to iteration always makes the program shorter and clearer

questions.title: Factorial Base Case
questions.description: A recursive factorial uses fact(n) = n * fact(n - 1). Which base case makes the method correct?
questions.Option1: When n is 0, return 0 and stop the recursion
questions.Option2: When n is 0 or 1, return 1 without calling fact again
questions.Option3: When n becomes negative, add 1 until it reaches zero again
questions.Option4: Factorial recursion needs no base case because n decreases by itself

questions.title: Naming the Recursive Case
questions.description: In sum(n) = n + sum(n - 1) with sum(0) = 0, what is the part n + sum(n - 1) called?
questions.Option3: The recursive case, which shrinks the problem toward the base case

questions.title: String Immutability During Recursive Calls
questions.description: A recursive method receives a String s and calls itself with s.substring(1). What happens to the original String object?
questions.Option1: Nothing changes in it, because Strings are immutable and substring returns a new String
questions.Option2: Its first character is permanently deleted from the original object
questions.Option3: The original String slowly becomes an empty string as calls proceed
questions.Option4: Java automatically converts the String into a char array to make room

questions.title: Recursive Array Sum Design
questions.description: You must write a method that returns the sum of an int array recursively. Which design is the standard recursive approach?
questions.Option1: Sort the array recursively first, then return its last element
questions.Option2: Pass the array plus an index, and combine the element at that index with the recursive sum of the remaining elements
questions.Option3: Convert the array to a String and add the character codes of its digits
questions.Option4: Create a new array half the size at every step until it is empty, never inspecting any element

questions.title: Effect of a Missing Base Case
questions.description: A recursive method has no base case and calls itself for every input. What is the most likely runtime outcome?
questions.Option1: The compiler rejects the program with a syntax error
questions.Option2: The method returns null after about one hundred calls
questions.Option3: The JVM detects the pattern and inserts a base case automatically
questions.Option4: The calls keep pushing stack frames until a StackOverflowError is thrown

questions.title: Memory Cost of Recursion Versus a Loop
questions.description: Compared to a simple loop that does the same work, recursion in Java usually:
questions.Option1: Runs faster because recursion avoids all loop bookkeeping
questions.Option2: Uses more memory because every call adds a new stack frame
questions.Option4: Is silently converted into a loop by the compiler
